mainTopic: How individual and communal offerings differ (תמורה, gender, making up missed offerings, overriding שבת), and whether נסכים may be brought at night
overview: This amud begins a משנה listing ways that an individual's offerings and communal offerings follow different rules. An individual's offering can make a תמורה, may come from male or female animals, and must be made up if it is missed. Communal offerings are only male and are not made up once their day passes. On the other hand, communal offerings override שבת and טומאה. רבי מאיר says the real rule is that any offering with a fixed time overrides them. The גמרא then tests the משנה's lines. It limits the תמורה rule to an original animal offering, and it explains how the male-and-female rule survives the cases of עולה, חטאת and אשם. Next it finds the source that missed מוספין are lost after their day, while their מנחה and נסכים may still be brought that night or the next day. This leads to a debate about whether נסכים can be offered at night. רמי בר חמא suggests one answer, רבא rejects it, and רב יוסף removes מנחת נסכים from a ברייתא. Finally, רב דימי hears from רבי יהושע בן לוי that נסכים are only by day and wants to send this to רב יוסף, a story that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Individual and communal offerings differ, starting with תמורה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה announces that individual and communal offerings each have rules the other lacks. Its first example is that an individual's offering can create a תמורה, but a communal offering cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are rules for an individual's offerings that do not apply to communal offerings, and rules for communal offerings that do not apply to an individual's offerings. An individual's offerings can make a תמורה; communal offerings cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a list of differences between offerings brought by one person and offerings brought by the whole community. The first difference is about תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמורה means someone tries to swap a regular animal for a holy one, and as a result the regular animal also becomes holy. The משנה says this only happens with an individual's offering. A communal offering does not make the swapped animal holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the text being learned)
Offerings brought by a single person
Offerings brought on behalf of the whole community
An animal swapped for a holy animal, which then becomes holy as well
Cause a swapped animal to become holy

phrases.english: MISHNA: There is, with individual offerings,
something that is not so with communal offerings,
and there is, with communal offerings,
something that is not so with individual offerings.
For individual offerings make a substitute,
but communal offerings do not make a substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת יָחִיד שֶׁאֵין בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual's offering can make a תמורה; a communal offering cannot.

steps.title: Males and females
steps.stepSummary: An individual's offerings can come from male or female animals. Communal offerings come only from males.
steps.simpleTranslation: Individual offerings apply to both males and females. Communal offerings apply only to males.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second difference between the two kinds of offerings: which animals they may come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some individual offerings come from female animals, so the category of individual offerings includes both males and females. Every communal offering comes from a male animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Apply, are found in
Male animals
Female animals

phrases.english: Individual offerings apply
to both males and females,
but communal offerings do not apply
except to males.

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד נוֹהֲגוֹת בֵּין בִּזְכָרִים בֵּין בִּנְקֵבוֹת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Individual offerings may be male or female; communal offerings are only male.

steps.title: Responsibility to make up the offering and its libations
steps.stepSummary: An individual is responsible to make up his offering and its נסכים. The community is not responsible to make up its offering or its נסכים, except that once the animal itself has been offered, its נסכים must still be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Individual offerings carry responsibility for themselves and for their libations. Communal offerings carry no responsibility for themselves or for their libations. But once the animal has been sacrificed, there is responsibility for its libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third difference: whether a missed or lost offering must be made up. It then adds one exception for communal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual who owes an offering must make it good later. A communal offering is tied to its day, so once that day passes it is not made up, and the same goes for its נסכים. The exception is when the animal was already offered: then its נסכים are still owed and can be brought afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Responsibility to replace or make up something
The flour offering and wine poured that come with an animal offering
The animal offering

steps.confusionAlert: The last line is not a contradiction. Communal נסכים are not made up when the whole offering was missed. They are owed only when the animal itself was already brought.

phrases.english: Individual offerings carry responsibility for themselves
and responsibility for their libations,
but communal offerings carry no responsibility for themselves
nor responsibility for their libations.
But they carry responsibility for their libations
once the animal offering has been sacrificed.

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד חַיָּיבִין בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן וּבְאַחְרָיוּת נִסְכֵּיהֶם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Individual offerings and their נסכים must be made up. Communal ones need not be, except that the נסכים are owed once the animal has been offered.

steps.title: Communal offerings override שבת and טומאה
steps.stepSummary: Now the משנה gives the other side: an advantage of communal offerings. Communal offerings are brought even on שבת and even in a state of טומאה, while an individual's offerings are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is something true of communal offerings that is not true of individual offerings. Communal offerings override שבת and טומאה, but individual offerings override neither שבת nor טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches to a rule where communal offerings have the advantage. They are brought on שבת and even when there is טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, sacrificing on שבת would involve forbidden work, and an impure state would block bringing an offering. Communal offerings push aside both of these limits. Individual offerings do not, according to this line of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Override, push aside
The Sabbath
Ritual impurity

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the target of רבי מאיר's challenge in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר מַה שֶּׁאֵין בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת יָחִיד
phrases.english: There is with communal offerings what is not so with individual offerings:
for communal offerings override
Shabbat and impurity,
but individual offerings do not override

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת הַטּוּמְאָה
phrases.english: neither Shabbat nor impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר מַה שֶּׁאֵין בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת יָחִיד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Communal offerings override שבת and טומאה; individual offerings do not.

steps.title: רבי מאיר points to individual offerings that override שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר objects to the last rule. The חביתין of the כהן גדול and the פר of יום הכפורים are individual offerings, yet they override שבת and טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: But aren't the כהן גדול's griddle-cake offerings and the bull of יום הכפורים individual offerings? And they do override שבת and טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר challenges the rule from the previous step by giving two counterexamples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both examples are brought by the כהן גדול as his own offering, so they count as individual offerings. Since they still override שבת and טומאה, the line between communal and individual cannot be the true rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
The daily griddle-cake flour offering of the כהן גדול
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכפורים

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
But aren't the High Priest's griddle-cakes
and the bull of Yom Kippur
individual offerings,
and yet they override Shabbat and impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that individual offerings never override שבת or טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two well-known individual offerings do override שבת and טומאה, so the communal/individual split fails.

steps.title: The real rule: a fixed time
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר gives the true principle. What overrides שבת and טומאה is an offering whose time is fixed, whether it is communal or individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it depends on whether its time is fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: Having knocked down the first rule, רבי מאיר replaces it with a new one: a fixed time is what counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתין are brought every day, and the פר is brought on יום הכפורים, so both have a set time. Any offering with a set time overrides שבת and טומאה. An offering with no set time can wait, so it does not override them.

keyTerms.meaning: Its time is fixed, it must be brought at a set time
Rather (introduces the corrected rule)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, what overrides שבת and טומאה is not whether an offering is communal. It is whether the offering has a fixed time.

phrases.english: Rather, it is whatever has a fixed time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי מאיר's challenge by offering a replacement principle
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An offering with a fixed time, whether communal or individual, overrides שבת and טומאה.

steps.title: Birds are individual offerings but make no substitute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule and asks whether it is a full rule, since birds are individual offerings yet do not make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said an individual's offering makes a substitute. Is that really a full rule? Birds are an individual's offering, and they do not make a substitute!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that a קרבן יחיד makes a תמורה. It then attacks it with the case of birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sounds like it covers every individual's offering. But bird offerings such as doves are brought by individuals, and everyone agrees they cannot make a תמורה. So the rule seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought by one person
A substitute: a regular animal someone tried to swap for a holy animal, which becomes holy itself
A general rule
Birds (bird offerings)

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Gemara: "An individual's offering makes a substitute," etc.
And is this a fixed rule?
But there are birds, which are an individual's offering,
and they do not make a substitute!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on a different line of the משנה, the rule about תמורה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's general statement that a קרבן יחיד makes a תמורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Birds are individual offerings, yet they cannot make a תמורה, so the rule is not true across the board.

steps.title: The rule is only about animals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's rule refers only to animal offerings, not bird offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה taught this, it was talking about animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה was only talking about animal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer narrows the משנה's rule rather than rejecting it. The rule was only ever about animal offerings, so birds are not a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: When it teaches (this), it means...
An animal (cattle, sheep or goats)

phrases.english: When it teaches this,
it is teaching about an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from birds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה covers every individual offering, including birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה covers only animal offerings.

steps.title: The offspring of an offering makes no substitute
steps.stepSummary: A ולד of a holy animal is an individual's offering, yet it does not make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the offspring is an individual's offering, and it does not make a substitute!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge: the baby animal born to a holy animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ולד is an animal, so the last answer does not cover it. It is brought as an individual's offering like its mother. Yet it does not make a תמורה, so the rule still looks too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring born to a holy animal, which is holy like its mother

phrases.english: But there is the offspring, which is an individual's offering,
and it does not make a substitute!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge that survives the "animals only" answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule, even when limited to animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ולד is an animal and an individual's offering, yet it makes no תמורה.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds that a ולד does make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this משנה? It is רבי יהודה's, who said the offspring does make a substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this משנה goes like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that a ולד makes no תמורה. רבי יהודה disagrees and holds that it does. According to him, the ולד fits the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי יהודה,
who said: the offspring makes a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ולד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ולד makes no תמורה, so it breaks the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, for whom a ולד does make a תמורה.

steps.title: A substitute itself makes no substitute
steps.stepSummary: A תמורה is offered as an individual's offering, yet a תמורה cannot make another תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the substitute itself is an individual's offering, and a substitute does not make a substitute!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge: the substitute animal itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה is a holy animal brought as an individual's offering. Yet it is a known rule that a תמורה cannot make another תמורה. So once again the משנה's rule seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: The substitute animal itself

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי תְּמוּרָה עַצְמָהּ, דְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד הִיא,
phrases.english: But there is the substitute itself, which is an individual's offering,
and a substitute does not make a substitute!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule about individual animal offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תמורה is an individual's animal offering, yet it cannot make a further תמורה.

steps.title: The rule is only about the original offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means only the original offering, not an animal that became holy through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה taught this, it was talking about the main, original offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה only means the original offering itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה is not the original offering. It only became holy because of the original one, so the משנה's rule does not cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: The main, original offering

phrases.english: When it teaches this, it is teaching about the main offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the תמורה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule covers every holy animal brought by an individual.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only the original offering.

steps.title: Now the משנה can follow the רבנן too
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה speaks only of the original offering, the ולד is excluded anyway, so the משנה can follow the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have reached this answer, you can even say the משנה follows the רבנן: it is only teaching about the main offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at the ולד challenge in light of the newest answer. It says we no longer need to assign the משנה to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ולד is also not the original offering, since it only became holy through its mother. So "original offering only" leaves the ולד out as well. That way the משנה fits even the רבנן, who say a ולד makes no תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this (answer)
You can even say

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule that a קרבן יחיד makes a תמורה covers only an original animal offering. Birds, a ולד, and a תמורה are all outside the rule, so the משנה can follow the רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: This step replaces the earlier answer about רבי יהודה (step 10). The משנה no longer has to follow him.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
you can even say it follows the רבנן,
phrases.notes: The רבנן here are the ones who argue with רבי יהודה and say a ולד makes no substitute.

phrases.english: since it is teaching about the main offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 12's answer to re-answer step 9 without needing step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "Original offering only" leaves out both the תמורה and the ולד, so the משנה can follow the רבנן.

steps.title: Quoting the line: individual offerings can be male or female
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which says an individual's offerings may be brought from males and from females.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: offerings of an individual apply to both males and females.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can examine it. This sets up the challenges that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts individual offerings with communal ones. Communal offerings are only male, but an individual's offerings can be male or female. The גמרא will now test how broad this claim really is.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings brought by a single person
Male animals
Female animals

phrases.english: Offerings of an individual apply
both with males and with females.

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד נוֹהֲגוֹת בֵּין בִּזְכָרִים בֵּין בִּנְקֵבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the תמורה discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual's offerings may be brought from either males or females.

steps.title: Challenge from the burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: Is this really a rule? An עולה is an individual's offering, yet it must be male.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a fixed rule? But an עולה is an individual's offering, and it comes only as a male, never as a female!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule by pointing to the עולה, which is only brought from male animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every individual offering could be male or female, the עולה would be a clear exception. An animal עולה must be male. So the משנה's statement looks too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: And is that a rule?
But there is the burnt offering, which is an individual's offering,
and it comes as a male, it does not come as a female!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the line just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that individual offerings can be male or female.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal עולה is an individual offering but must be male, so it seems to contradict the rule.

steps.title: Answer: a bird burnt offering can be either
steps.stepSummary: There is the bird עולה, which can be male or female, as a ברייתא teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is the bird burnt offering. A ברייתא teaches: being unblemished and being male are required for animals, but not for birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the עולה category does include a female option, because a bird עולה can be either male or female.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the requirement to be male applies only to animals, not birds. So within the עולה category, an individual can bring a female, as a bird. That is enough to fit the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering brought from a bird
Being unblemished
Being male

phrases.english: There is the bird burnt offering,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
Being unblemished and being male apply to an animal,
but being unblemished and being male do not apply to birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the עולה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the category has a sub-type that fits the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an animal עולה must be male; a bird עולה can be female, so the עולה category fits the rule.

steps.title: Challenge from the sin offering
steps.stepSummary: A חטאת is an individual's offering, yet it comes as a female and not as a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a חטאת is an individual's offering, and it comes only as a female, never as a male!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the opposite problem: the ordinary individual חטאת must be female.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עולה was a problem because it seemed male-only. The חטאת seems female-only, so it also looks like an exception to 'both males and females.'

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering

phrases.english: But there is the sin offering, which is an individual's offering,
and it comes as a female, it does not come as a male?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the same rule, from the other direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that individual offerings can be male or female.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ordinary individual חטאת is only female, so it seems to contradict the rule.

steps.title: Answer: the king's goat is male
steps.stepSummary: There is the שעיר נשיא, an individual חטאת that is brought as a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is the goat of the נשיא, who brings a male.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חטאת category does have a male option: the נשיא brings a male goat as his חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the bird עולה, this shows that within the חטאת category an individual sometimes brings a male. So the category as a whole includes both genders.

keyTerms.meaning: The male goat brought as a חטאת by the king

phrases.english: There is the goat of the king,
who brings a male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the חטאת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the category has a sub-type that fits the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The individual חטאת is always female.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נשיא's חטאת is a male goat, so the חטאת category includes a male.

steps.title: Challenge from the guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: An individual's אשם comes only as a male, with no female version at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the individual's אשם, which comes as a male and never as a female!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a harder case: the אשם, which has no female version anywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike עולה and חטאת, the אשם has no sub-type that comes from the other gender. So the earlier kind of answer will not work here.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual's guilt offering

phrases.english: But there is the individual's guilt offering,
which comes as a male, does not come as a female?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge that the earlier style of answer cannot solve.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that individual offerings can be male or female.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אשם is always male and has no female sub-type, so it truly breaks the rule.

steps.title: Answer: only offerings shared by individual and community
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only means offerings that exist both for individuals and for the community. An אשם is never communal, so it is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the רבנן said this, they meant an offering that exists both for an individual and for the community. An אשם exists for an individual but not for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing what the משנה is talking about: only offerings that come both as individual and as communal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה compares individual offerings with communal ones. That comparison only makes sense for offerings that exist in both forms. Since there is no communal אשם, it falls outside the משנה's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Equal; here, found in both settings
The community as a whole
Guilt offering

phrases.english: When the Rabbis said it,
they meant an offering that is equal
both for an individual and for the community;
a guilt offering exists for an individual,
but for the community it does not exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן קׇרְבָּן דְּשָׁוֵי בֵּין בְּיָחִיד בֵּין בְּצִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the אשם.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule covers every individual offering, including the אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only covers offerings that exist for both individuals and the community; the אשם is not one of them.

steps.title: Second answer: the משנה says only some offerings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה never said 'all offerings,' only 'there are offerings,' meaning שלמים, which can be male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: does the משנה say 'all offerings'? It says 'there are among the offerings.' Which ones? שלמים, where a person may bring a female or a male, as he wishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer: read the משנה's wording carefully. It only claims that some individual offerings can be male or female.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה opens with 'יש בקרבנות', 'there are among the offerings', not 'כל קרבנות', 'all offerings.' So it is enough that one kind, שלמים, can be either gender. The עולה, חטאת and אשם challenges no longer matter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say' — introduces another answer
'There are among the offerings' — only some
Peace offerings, which may be male or female

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the אשם problem: either the משנה only means offerings found for both individual and community, or its wording, 'יש', only claims that some offerings, namely שלמים, can be either gender.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Does it teach "all offerings"?
It teaches "there are among the offerings,"
and what are they?
Peace offerings,
and if he wants, he brings a female,
and if he wants, he brings a male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same אשם challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה claims every individual offering can be male or female.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only claims that some offerings, namely שלמים, can be either gender.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the rule about making up offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks where we learn that communal offerings are not made up once their time has passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said individual offerings must be made up, and so on. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts two groups. Individual offerings are made up if they were missed, but communal offerings are not. The question 'מנא לן' focuses mainly on the surprising half: why a missed communal offering is simply lost.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings brought by an individual person
Responsibility to replace or make up an offering that was not brought
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Offerings of an individual: one is obligated to make them up, etc.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of male and female offerings and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that missed communal offerings are not made up.

steps.title: The whole day works for the מוספין, but once the day passes they are lost
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'דבר יום' that the whole day is valid for the מוספין, and from 'ביומו' that once the day ends, they are not made up.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'Each day's matter' teaches that the whole day is fit for the מוספין. 'On its day' teaches that if the day passed and they were not brought, there is no obligation to make them up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads two parts of one פסוק. The extra word 'ביומו' limits the מוסף to its own day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דבר יום' shows the מוסף may be brought at any point during the day. 'ביומו' adds a limit: the offering belongs only to its own day. So once that day passes, there is nothing left to make up, which is the משנה's rule for communal offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The additional communal offerings brought on שבת, ראש חודש and יום טוב
'Each day's matter on its day' (ויקרא 23:37), the פסוק being explained
On its own day; read here as a limit to that day only

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"Each day's matter"
teaches that the entire day is fit for the additional offerings,
"on its day"
teaches that if the day has passed
and they did not bring them,
one is not obligated to make them up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ביומו' limits the מוסף to its own day, so a missed one is not made up.

steps.title: Maybe the נסכים are also lost once the day passes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: perhaps even the נסכים of an animal that was already brought are lost once the day ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that there is no obligation to make up their libations, even though the animal offering was already brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests a possible but wrong idea, so that it can correct it in the next line. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that a missed מוסף is gone after its day. Someone might stretch this rule to the מנחה and נסכים that go with the animal, even if the animal itself was brought on time. The ברייתא asks whether they are also lost.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think'; it introduces a mistaken idea that will be corrected
Wine libations poured with an animal offering
The animal offering itself

phrases.english: One might think one would not be obligated
to make up their libations,
even though the animal offering was already brought?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּת נִסְכֵּיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the rule of step 23 also covers the נסכים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the נסכים of an animal that was already offered also lost once the day ends?

steps.title: The מנחה and נסכים may be brought that night or the next day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the phrase 'מנחתם ונסכיהם' that the מנחה and נסכים can still be brought at night or even on the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'their meal offerings and their libations' — even at night. 'Their meal offerings and their libations' — even the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The מנחה and נסכים are not lost when the day ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מנחתם ונסכיהם' are read twice. The first time teaches that the מנחה and נסכים may be brought at night. The second time teaches that they may be brought even the next day. So the 'one day only' limit applies to the animal, not to the מנחה and נסכים that go with it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches'; it introduces the proof that corrects the mistaken idea
'Their meal offerings and their libations' (במדבר 29)
On the next day

steps.whatToRemember: A missed communal מוסף is not made up after its day. But if the animal was brought, its מנחה and נסכים can still be brought that night or the next day.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Their meal offerings and their libations" — even at night,
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:37. The same phrase is read twice, and each reading teaches something new.

phrases.english: "Their meal offerings and their libations" — even on the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled phrase 'מנחתם ונסכיהם' allows the מנחה and נסכים to be brought at night and on the next day.

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns it from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש brings a different source for the rule: the words 'מלבד שבתות ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: we learn it from here: 'מלבד שבתות ה׳', besides the שבתות of ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives another פסוק as the source for the rule about the נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'מלבד שבתות ה׳' as speaking about a יום טוב that falls the day after שבת. On that יום טוב, the מנחה and נסכים left over from שבת's מוסף may still be brought. This is a second source for the idea that the נסכים may be brought on a later day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From here'; it introduces a different source
'Besides the שבתות of ה׳' (ויקרא 23:38)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: from here:
"Besides the Shabbatot of the Lord."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:38. He reads it as allowing שבת's נסכים to be brought on a יום טוב that comes right after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source from the ברייתא's 'מנחתם ונסכיהם'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מלבד שבתות ה׳' teaches that שבת's מנחה and נסכים may be brought on the יום טוב that follows.

steps.title: Why both verses are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that each verse alone would teach only part of the rule, so both are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both verses are needed. If the Torah wrote only 'מלבד שבתות ה׳', I would think the leftover offerings may be brought the next day but not that night, so it wrote 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם'. If it wrote only 'מנחתם ונסכיהם', I would think they may be brought that night but not the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we need both sources: the ברייתא's 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' and ריש לקיש's 'מלבד שבתות ה׳'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מלבד שבתות ה׳' alone would allow only the next day, because the animal itself could not be brought at night. 'מנחתם ונסכיהם' alone would allow only the night right after. Together they allow both the night and the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary: both sources are needed
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
I would have said: a mistaken first thought
Besides the Sabbaths of the Lord (ויקרא 23:38)
Their meal offerings and their libations

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two verses up. 'מלבד שבתות ה׳' alone would have allowed only the next day. 'מנחתם ונסכיהם' alone would have allowed only that night.

phrases.english: And both are needed, for if the Merciful One had written only
"Besides the Sabbaths of the Lord," I would have said:
by day, yes; at night, no.
So the verse says, "And their meal offerings and their libations."
And if the Merciful One had written "their meal offerings and their libations"
and had not written "Besides the Sabbaths of the Lord,"
I would have said: on its night, yes,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, means 'its night,' the night right after.

phrases.english: but the next day, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why ריש לקיש's source does not make the ברייתא's source extra, and why the ברייתא's source does not make his extra.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each verse covers a different time, the night or the next day, so both verses are needed.

steps.title: Why would night be better than the next day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we would have thought the night is allowed but the next day is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference between the night and the next day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the second half of the explanation. Why would 'מנחתם ונסכיהם' alone have allowed only the night and not the next day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, the night and the next day both come after the offering's proper time. So why would one be allowed and the other not?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
On its night: the night right after the day
By day: here, the next day

phrases.english: And what is the difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reasoning behind the second half of the צריכותא in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why we would have thought that the night counts but the next day does not.

steps.title: With קדשים, the night follows the day
steps.stepSummary: With קדשים, the night after a day counts as part of that day. So without the second verse we would allow only that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because with sacrifices, the night follows the day before it. That is why both verses are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that with קדשים, the night belongs to the day before it. That is why we would have allowed only the night, and so both verses are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים, the night still counts as part of the day before it. So we would have treated that night as an extension of the offering's day and allowed only it. The extra verse teaches that even the next day is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrifices and holy offerings
The night follows the day: it counts as part of the day before it
They are needed: both verses

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's verse and ריש לקיש's verse together allow late מנחות and נסכים both that night and the next day.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דִּבְקָדָשִׁים לַיְלָה הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: Because with sacrifices, the night follows the day,
so both are needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דִּבְקָדָשִׁים לַיְלָה הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because with קדשים the night follows the day, we would have allowed only the night. So we need the second verse to allow the next day.

steps.title: Can libations be offered at night at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that נסכים can be offered at night. It starts quoting a ברייתא about which items may burn at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: But are libations offered at night? We learned: I only know about items that are normally offered at night, like limbs and fats, which are offered after sunset and keep burning all night long.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what was just said, that נסכים may be brought at night. It begins quoting a ברייתא to show that this seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא begins with items that really are offered at night, like the limbs and fats. It is setting up a contrast with daytime items, which come next. That is where the problem for נסכים will show up.

keyTerms.meaning: Libations: wine and its accompanying meal offering
I only know: the verse clearly covers only this case
Limbs of an עולה burned on the altar
Fats of offerings burned on the altar
Are consumed by the altar fire

phrases.english: But are libations offered at night?
But we learned: I only know about
items that are normally offered at night,
phrases.notes: This comes from the words 'all night' in ויקרא 6:2.

phrases.english: such as limbs and fats,
which are offered after sunset
and keep burning all night long.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim from steps 25 and 27 that the מנחה and נסכים may be brought at night.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that leftover מנחות and נסכים may be offered at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא treats מנחת נסכים as a daytime item, so how can it be offered at night?

steps.title: The ברייתא lists daytime items, including מנחת נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with items normally offered by day, among them מנחת נסכים, and seems to ask how they can be brought up after sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: Items normally offered by day, such as the handful, the frankincense, and the meal offering of libations, from where do we know that one may bring them up after sunset?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. This is the line that actually matters for the challenge, because it lists מנחת נסכים as a daytime item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא calls מנחת נסכים a daytime item, that is the proof against offering נסכים at night. The question 'from where?' is finished only later, in step 33.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a meal offering and burned
Frankincense burned with a meal offering
The meal offering that comes with libations

phrases.english: Items that are normally offered by day,
such as the handful, the frankincense, and the meal offering of libations,
that one may bring them up after sunset?
phrases.notes: The 'from where do we know' part of this question shows up a bit later, in step 33.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: That מנחת נסכים is not normally offered at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists מנחת נסכים among items normally offered by day

steps.title: Daytime items after sunset?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the ברייתא's wording: how can daytime items be brought up after sunset?
steps.simpleTranslation: After sunset, could you think so?! But you just said these are items normally offered by day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops in the middle of the ברייתא. The wording 'after sunset' contradicts the ברייתא's own description of these items as daytime items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If these items belong to the day, they cannot be put on the altar after sunset. So the ברייתא's wording cannot be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? This is an expression of surprise
From sunset: after the sun has set
But you said

phrases.english: After sunset, could you really think so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִיקְרַב בַּיּוֹם נִינְהוּ!
phrases.english: But you said these are items normally offered by day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 31.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Daytime items cannot be placed on the altar after sunset, so the wording contradicts itself.

steps.title: Read it as 'with sunset': placed just before, burned at night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really means daytime items placed on the altar just as the sun sets may burn through the night. This is learned from 'זאת תורת העולה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as 'with sunset': from where do we know that they may keep burning all night? The verse says, 'This is the law of the burnt offering.' This includes them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects the reading of the ברייתא. The daytime items are placed on the altar right at sunset, and the verse 'זאת תורת העולה' allows them to keep burning all night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the burning continues at night. The actual placing on the altar still happens in the daytime. This sharpens the challenge from step 30. Even מנחת נסכים is not truly offered at night, so how could leftover נסכים be brought then?

keyTerms.meaning: With sunset: right at the moment the sun sets
The verse teaches
This is the law of the burnt offering (ויקרא 6:2)
It included: the verse widens the rule

steps.confusionAlert: This answer fixes the wording of the ברייתא. It does not answer the challenge of step 30. In fact, it makes the challenge stronger, because מנחת נסכים is placed on the altar only by day.

phrases.english: Rather, read it as 'with sunset,'
so that they keep burning all night: from where do we know this?
The verse says, "This is the law of the burnt offering": it included them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows placing daytime items on the altar after sunset.
steps.terutzMaskana: Daytime items are placed on the altar right at sunset and may burn through the night, based on 'זאת תורת העולה'.

steps.title: The ברייתא still says נסכים are by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its difficulty. The ברייתא lists נסכים among the things brought by day, but the verse seemed to allow them at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that נסכים are brought by day!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ברייתא has been explained, the גמרא goes back to its main problem. That same ברייתא puts נסכים on the daytime list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in step 25, the ברייתא read the phrase 'מנחתם ונסכיהם' as allowing the מנחה and נסכים to be brought at night, the night after the day the קרבן was brought. But this other ברייתא counts מנחת נסכים among the daytime items. So the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. This sets aside side issues and goes back to the main problem.
The flour offering and wine that go with an animal קרבן
By day, during daytime

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches that libations are by day!
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from the last few steps, which lists מנחת נסכים among the daytime items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ברייתא's wording is settled, the גמרא goes back to its main challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that נסכים may be brought at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists מנחת נסכים as a daytime item, which goes against reading the verse as allowing them at night.

steps.title: Making it holy versus bringing it on the altar
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא answers that the night verse is about the offering becoming holy, while the ברייתא is about offering it on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: This is no problem. Here it is about becoming holy; there it is about being offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא settles the clash by saying the two sources talk about two different actions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse that seemed to allow night means only that the נסכים become holy at night, when placed in a holy vessel. The ברייתא's rule is about actually putting them on the altar, which must wait for day. So nothing clashes.

keyTerms.meaning: It is no problem. Used to open an answer.
Here... there. Splits the two sources into two different cases.
To become holy (consecrated)
To be offered on the altar

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
It is not difficult —
here, to become consecrated; there, to be sacrificed.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the night verse, which is only about the offering becoming holy. 'There' is the ברייתא, which is about bringing it on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא — כָּאן לִיקְדַּשׁ, כָּאן לִיקְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 34
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into two different actions (becoming holy versus being offered)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse and the ברייתא disagree about whether נסכים may be offered at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: נסכים become holy at night but are offered only by day.

steps.title: רבא: becoming holy and being offered go together
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רמי בר חמא's split. A ברייתא teaches that an offering becomes holy only at the times it may be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If they become holy, they can be offered! For a ברייתא teaches: This is the rule: whatever is offered by day becomes holy only by day. Whatever is offered at night becomes holy at night. Whatever is offered both by day and at night becomes holy both by day and at night!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the answer. He shows from a ברייתא that you cannot split 'becoming holy' from 'being offered'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties the two together: an offering becomes holy only at a time when it may be brought. So if נסכים can become holy at night, they can also be offered at night. That puts us back at the original clash with the daytime list.

keyTerms.meaning: Once they are holy, they may be brought on the altar
This is the general rule
Becomes holy (consecrated)
Whatever is offered on the altar

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If they become consecrated, then they may also be sacrificed,
for it is taught in a ברייתא: This is the principle:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַקָּרֵב בַּיּוֹם — אֵין קָדוֹשׁ אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: Whatever is sacrificed by day becomes consecrated only by day,
and whatever is sacrificed at night becomes consecrated at night,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בְּלַיְלָה — קָדוֹשׁ בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בַּלַּיְלָה!
phrases.english: and whatever is sacrificed both by day and at night becomes consecrated both by day and at night!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִיקְדָּשׁ קָדְשִׁי קָרוֹבֵי מִיקָּרְבִי, וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 35
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's split between becoming holy and being offered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא makes the time for becoming holy match the time for being offered. So the two cannot be pulled apart.

steps.title: רב יוסף: take מנחת נסכים out of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף solves the problem by removing 'מנחת נסכים' from the ברייתא's list of daytime items.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: Remove 'מנחת נסכים' from this ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the split did not work, רב יוסף takes a different route. He says the ברייתא should not list מנחת נסכים at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף keeps the verse as allowing נסכים at night, for both becoming holy and being offered. He fixes the ברייתא instead: once מנחת נסכים is off its daytime list, the clash is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Drops the earlier answer and offers a new one.
Remove it, take it out of the text
A teaching from the time of the תנאים. Here it means the ברייתא.
The flour offering that comes along with the wine of the נסכים

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers were tried. רמי בר חמא's split (holy at night, offered by day) was rejected by רבא, so רב יוסף deletes מנחת נסכים from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Delete 'meal offering of libations' from this baraita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that failed in Step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing an item from the ברייתא's list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא really lists מנחת נסכים as daytime only.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should not include מנחת נסכים. נסכים may be brought at night.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: נסכים with a קרבן are only by day
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי finds רב ירמיה teaching, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, that נסכים coming with an animal קרבן are offered only by day. This is learned from placing them next to שלמים in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רב ירמיה sitting and saying in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: From where do we know that נסכים coming with a קרבן are offered only by day? The verse says 'and your libations and your peace offerings'. Just as שלמים are by day, so נסכים are by day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching comes in that seems to back up the ברייתא's original wording: נסכים that come with a קרבן are offered only by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places נסכים right next to שלמים, and שלמים are offered only by day. So נסכים are also only by day. This casts doubt on רב יוסף's deletion, because a real source supports listing נסכים as daytime only.

keyTerms.meaning: When he went up, from בבל to ארץ ישראל
From where do we know? Asks for the source in the פסוק.
The verse teaches, introducing the פסוק as the source
That come along with the animal קרבן
Just as... so too... A comparison drawn from placing two things side by side in a פסוק.

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching seems to undo רב יוסף's deletion. It shows that a real source supports the ברייתא's daytime rule for נסכים.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi ascended,
he found Rav Yirmeya sitting

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: and saying in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
From where do we know that libations that come with an animal offering
are sacrificed only by day?
The verse states: 'and your libations, and your peace offerings' —

phrases.aramaic: מָה שְׁלָמִים בַּיּוֹם, אַף נְסָכִים בַּיּוֹם.
phrases.english: just as peace offerings are by day, so too libations are by day.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק רַב דִּימִי, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a teaching that goes against רב יוסף's deletion in Step 37
steps.raayaObject: That נסכים coming with a קרבן are offered only by day, as the ברייתא's original wording says
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'וּלְנִסְכֵּיכֶם וּלְשַׁלְמֵיכֶם', which places נסכים next to שלמים

steps.title: רב דימי wants to send the teaching to רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says he would send this teaching by letter to רב יוסף, if he finds someone to write it. The sentence continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: If I find someone who writes a letter, I would send it to רב יוסף,
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up the next move. רב דימי wants this teaching to reach רב יוסף, because it goes against רב יוסף's deletion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף was in בבל and had removed מנחת נסכים from the ברייתא. רב דימי sees that רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching backs the original wording, so he wants to tell רב יוסף. What he would write comes in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter
I would send it to him

phrases.english: He said: If I find someone who writes a letter,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב דימי, reacting to what he just heard from רב ירמיה.

phrases.english: I would send it to Rav Yosef,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב דימי wants to apply the teaching of Step 38 to רב יוסף's view in Step 37
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב דימי plans to tell רב יוסף about the teaching that נסכים coming with a קרבן are only by day.
